cost_reported: Opus run 0.68 USD in API fees; with LLM latency an Opus run took 39% (Sonnet 174%) longer wall-clock than the 80-epoch recipe
evidence_notes: The LLM meta-learner is the paper's method (p.1-2): it reads weight snapshots and statistics with tools and submits a Python program that returns a complete weight state at virtual-epoch slots, validated before acceptance (p.4-5), so code_or_tensor_tool, closed loop, whole network. No preregistration is mentioned; code and transcripts 'will be made publicly available upon publication' (p.13). AI-use disclosure says AI improved code, debugged and edited text (p.14); the LLM rediscovered snapshot averaging and a fixed averaging rule matched it (p.1, p.12); largest target ResNet-18 at 11.22M (Table 1, p.7).
